+import typing
+
+from sqlalchemy.engine.row import Row
+
+from databases.interfaces import Record as RecordInterface
+
+
+class Record(RecordInterface):
+    """
+    Wrapper around a SQLAlchemy :class:`Row` that restores the legacy
+    (pre-2.0) mapping-style access patterns used by ``databases``.
+
+    SQLAlchemy 2.0 changed :class:`Row` so that it only behaves as a
+    sequence; mapping behaviour (``row["column"]``, ``dict(row)`` etc.)
+    must go through ``row._mapping``.  This wrapper exposes the familiar
+    hybrid mapping/sequence interface on top of the new-style Row.
+    """
+
+    __slots__ = ("_row",)
+
+    def __init__(self, row: Row) -> None:
+        self._row = row
+
+    @property
+    def _mapping(self) -> typing.Mapping:
+        return self._row._mapping
+
+    def keys(self) -> typing.KeysView:
+        return self._mapping.keys()
+
+    def values(self) -> typing.ValuesView:
+        return self._mapping.values()
+
+    def items(self) -> typing.ItemsView:
+        return self._mapping.items()
+
+    def __getitem__(self, key: typing.Any) -> typing.Any:
+        if isinstance(key, (int, slice)):
+            return self._row[key]
+        return self._mapping[key]
+
+    def __iter__(self) -> typing.Iterator:
+        return iter(self._row)
+
+    def __len__(self) -> int:
+        return len(self._row)
+
+    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> typing.Any:
+        return getattr(self._row, name)

The repo (encode/databases) was written against SQLAlchemy 1.4's internal row API, which SQLAlchemy 2.0 removed. I fixed the source code to work with the installed SQLAlchemy 2.0.52:

Replaced the removed SQLAlchemy 1.4 construction `Row(metadata, metadata._processors, metadata._keymap, Row._default_key_style, row)` (which referenced the now-deleted `Row._default_key_style` class attribute and 5-arg constructor) with the SQLAlchemy 2.0 form `Row(metadata, metadata._processors, metadata._key_to_index, row)`, wrapped in the new `Record`.
